name: paxos
system: Paxos agreement (IJCAR source, finite TLC ballot projection)

property.name: Consistency
property.statement: no two distinct values are chosen

calibration.n0_rule: first adjacent under-cap successful TLC pair that brackets median theorem+own-corollary totals; select log-nearest N>=3 within factor 2, require a chosen-value witness at each N
calibration.heap_profile: observed implicit 14247MB heap, mechanism unknown; -fp/-seed random per run (protocol 4.4 not satisfied); curve is exploratory, not a pinned-profile row set

heap_profile.decision: 14 GiB (14336 MiB), chosen over 8 GiB at the stage-2 checkpoint
heap_profile.rationale: 14336 MiB is the pinned requested ceiling (-Xmx14336m). On the pinned JRE (OpenJDK 1.8.0_504, ParallelGC) the TLC banner reports usable heap ~8/9 of the request -- measured 12743 MB here -- NOT 14336 and NOT the exploratory 14247. The user chose this value with that consequence stated: a different, ~10% smaller effective heap than the exploratory rows, accepted as a distinct configuration.
heap_profile.caveat: The historical 14247 MB banner corresponds to about -Xmx16028m under the measured relation (16028 x 8/9 = 14247.1). The pinned JRE's own default MaxHeapSize measured 16027 MiB -- one MiB below that, so its banner would round to 14246. The origin is therefore the JVM's default max heap (one quarter of this host's ~62 GiB) seen through survivor-space accounting, resolved to within about 1 MiB rather than exactly. So 14 GiB does not reproduce the historical launcher conditions; reproducing the historical banner needs about -Xmx16028m.
heap_profile.delivery: must reach the TLC child as JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Xmx14336m; tlc -Xmx was observed rejected; the wrapper execs Java with TLC args after the main class
heap_profile.row_requirement: rows record tlc_profile.requested {heap_mib, fp_index, seed} with explicit null for each omitted flag, tlc_profile.heap_delivery (the JVM's own 'Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: -Xmx<M>m' witness, or null), and tlc_profile.observed with the parsed banner values -- the pickup line, not the banner, attests the heap
heap_profile.measured_demand: observed exploratory N=7 RSS peak 5535.5 MB (whole-process used memory); fixed-profile memory demand is NOT yet measured. Comparing RSS with the 14 GiB java-heap maximum is an illustrative ratio, not evidence of headroom, and it does not establish that no other limit (offheap, disk, host) binds.
heap_profile.established: N=7 reached 10,850,698 distinct states and timed out at the 7200 s cap rather than dying on a resource error; that is the only resource claim stage 1 supports
heap_profile.measured_relationship: banner effective heap ~ 8/9 x -Xmx, round to nearest: the banner reports Runtime.maxMemory(), i.e. -Xmx minus one survivor space. Measured on the pinned JRE: -Xmx4096m->3641MB, 5000m->4444MB, 9216m->8192MB, 14336m->12743MB, 16384m->14564MB. This is a FIT, not an exact identity - a floor() rule fails two of these samples and the JVM's heap alignment is the real mechanism.
